transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Toby Li (Redwood Product), Jordan Park (Acme PM), Priya Reddy (Acme ML), Nate Flores (Acme Security), Marta Silva (Acme DevOps)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give a 35-40 minute walkthrough of our structured output and function-calling flow and then leave time for Q&A. quick intro, I'm Alex, AE, Samira will drive the demo.
[00:12] Samira: hi everybody, thanks. I'll share my screen — starting with the API JSON mode. so the idea here is you can provide a schema and the model will attempt to emit JSON that validates to that schema. we also demonstrate how Redwood can enforce it and fall back if the model drifts.
[00:28] Jordan: curious — when you say "enforce" do you mean post-processing validation or the runtime actually rejects nonconformant tokens?
[00:35] Samira: good question. it's mostly a two-layer pattern: first, we bias generation with schema-aware prompts and constrained decoding when supported by the model; second, the Console/runtime validates the output and can either repair (beam-rescore + regen) or call a correction tool. you can configure strictness by route.
[00:52] Priya: is this available on both hosted and dedicated? we want the pilot on dedicated GPUs.
[00:58] Alex: yes both. dedicated gives you predictable latency and isolation — we'll show model variants and a canary rollout in the Console.
[01:07] Samira: demo: switching to the Console. here is a route configured for "invoice-extract" with JSON schema attached. schema includes fields: invoice_id (string), total_amount (number), currency (string), line_items (array of objects). I'll trigger a sample request from the Console playground.
[01:30] [Samira types, runs example]
[01:34] Samira: you can see the response in JSON mode. note the timestamped tokens stream but the final payload validates. we also highlight which tokens were regenerated when the validator ran.
[01:47] Marta: when the validator regenerates, do you incur extra tokens on billing?
[01:52] Samira: yes any additional model calls are billed; Redwood Optimize can estimate expected unit cost and suggest batching or KV cache keys to reduce tokens.
[02:02] Toby: also important — you can enable server-side correction tools: e.g., a small deterministic parser that converts dates/currencies before returning to the client, that avoids another full model call.
[02:14] Jordan: show function/tool calling please — our backend needs to map model outputs to internal APIs.
[02:19] Samira: switching to function-calling demo. we define a function signature for create_invoice(payload JSON schema) and show how the model can return a "function_call" object with arguments matching the schema. console shows the mapping and you can opt to auto-execute or review.
[02:36] [Samira runs function call example]
[02:39] Samira: here model returned function_call with args; Console shows a preview and a validation status — green if it matched schema. If mismatched, we show diffs and either a patch or a rerun option.
[02:52] Priya: what about hallucinated fields or unexpected extra fields?
[02:56] Samira: validators catch unexpected fields; by default extra fields are dropped and logged. you can configure to surface them to the user or to fail the request. logs go to the Console and to your audit logs for debugging.
[03:08] Nate: security question — where are these logs stored? do they include raw PII?
[03:12] Alex: logs live in customer-controlled storage for Private deployments; for hosted we store them encrypted with KMS and can redact sensitive fields; we have config to disable storing raw request bodies. we'll send the security pack with exact retention policies.
[03:25] Marta: we need SSO, SAML, and RBAC mapped to our AD groups.
[03:29] Alex: supported — Console integrates with SAML/SSO and has role-based permissions for routes and rollout access.
[03:36] Jordan: back to function-calling: can we call internal tools that require additional headers/credentials?
[03:40] Samira: yes you set up connectors that inject credentials at call-time in the Private deployment or via a secure vault integration in Dedicated. Redwood never surfaces secrets in the model prompt.
[03:50] Priya: curious about schema complexity — nested arrays, optional unions etc. any limits?
[03:55] Samira: we recommend keeping the schema reasonably sized; large deeply nested schemas can increase decoding complexity. for complex types we suggest emitting a compact intermediate structure and post-process with a deterministic transformer. file size wise it's fine, but performance may vary by model. we'll show Optimize recommendations shortly.
[04:15] [Samira pulls up Optimize panel]
[04:18] Samira: Optimize suggests batching profiles, quantization level (e.g., int8 vs q4_K), and KV caching keys. for invoice-extract the common prefix is large (the invoice header) so prefix caching reduces tokens significantly. here the estimated cost dropped by ~38% with a suggested batching window.
[04:37] Jordan: nice — that helps with unit economics. do you have real benchmarks on RBC or 2k sequence lengths?
[04:44] Samira: we have benchmark sheets; we'll run a pilot with your sample prompts at 2k and 4k lengths. dedicated capacity lets you pick GPUs and we can pin model quantization variants.
[04:55] Priya: model compatibility — we currently use an internal Llama-derivative; can Redwood route calls to that?
[05:01] Alex: we can host your model in Private or Dedicated if it's compatible with our runtime; otherwise you can use Redwood-hosted models. we support custom model upload for Private and some Dedicated configurations.
[05:13] Nate: for compliance we need audit trails showing which model version and which user triggered a route, and immutable logs for 12 months.
[05:20] Samira: Console has per-request metadata — tokens, model version, rollout id, user id — and logs can be exported to your SIEM. retention is configurable; we'll include that in the security pack.
[05:34] Jordan: any guardrails for safety — e.g., block certain PII or ensure currency normalization?
[05:40] Samira: yes guardrails can be route-level filters: block patterns, named-entity detectors, or deterministic post-processors. plus you can add a secondary regression test suite tied to prompt sets so a rollout fails if extracted values drop below expected F1.
[05:55] Alex: showing the Eval and rollout integration: here's an eval that runs against a corpus of labeled invoices; you can see metrics over time and set a rollout rule to stop if quality regresses.
[06:08] [Samira shows a rollout config: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with auto-rollback]
[06:16] Marta: on-network: what's the VPC setup if we go Dedicated in our cloud account?
[06:20] Alex: Dedicated can be VPC peered or deployed inside your account depending on the plan; we'll share architecture diagrams.
[06:27] Priya: let's talk edge cases — what if the model returns a number as a string and schema expects number?
[06:32] Samira: the validator will cast basic types when safe (e.g., numeric strings) if you enable permissive mode; in strict mode it fails and triggers a correction flow. you can map those behaviors per-route.
[06:45] Jordan: how do we handle multi-step flows where the model calls multiple internal functions in sequence?
[06:50] Samira: we support chained function calls: the model can emit function_call for step one, Redwood can auto-execute then feed results back as context for next step. the Console shows the chain and execution logs.
[07:03] Priya: rate limits — if we scale to thousands of calls per second what does dedicated throughput look like?
[07:09] Alex: depends on GPU type and model; we'll propose profiles in the pilot SOW. Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity.
[07:18] Nate: more security: can we have field-level encryption for certain columns in the logs?
[07:23] Samira: for Private yes; for Hosted we offer tokenization/redaction and encryption at rest with KMS. field-level encryption is part of the enterprise package.
[07:33] Jordan: show an example where schema enforcement forced a regeneration and the model succeeded after correction.
[07:38] Samira: demo run: initial generation omitted line_items prices; validator flagged missing required field, Console triggered a focused regen with a constrained prompt and the model returned a patched JSON that validated. you can see the diff and extra tokens used.
[07:58] [short pause as Samira toggles logs]
[08:02] Priya: are these diffs exportable to our error tracking? we want to link failures to Sentry / internal issue trackers.
[08:08] Samira: yes diffs and evidence payloads can be streamed to your webhook; we also support exporting to S3 or SIEM connectors.
[08:18] Jordan: licensing and pricing — what's the model for Dedicated + Optimize?
[08:23] Alex: high level: Dedicated has a base monthly capacity fee plus per-token compute for overage in some plans. Optimize and long-term storage are add-ons. we'll send a tailored estimate based on your expected qps and token lengths.
[08:37] Marta: do you have prebuilt SDKs? our backend is in Go and Python.
[08:41] Samira: yes SDKs in Python, Go, Node; we also have example function-calling integrations and a notebook we can share.
[08:48] Jordan: any integration with our CI for automated evals?
[08:51] Samira: Eval results can be pulled via API and integrated into CI to gate rollouts.
[08:56] Alex: ok time for Q&A — Jordan or Priya anything else?
[08:59] Jordan: quick—what's the timeline for a pilot? we want to start next week ideally.
[09:03] Alex: we can target a 2-week pilot: day 0 setup, day 1 benchmark, week 1 optimizations and week 2 validation; we'll send SOW.
[09:11] Priya: we'll share sample prompts and schemas tonight.
[09:14] Nate: please include data deletion guarantees in the security pack.
[09:18] Alex: will do.
[09:20] Toby: one last product note — we have a model-version compatibility table and a fallback policy engine that will route to simpler models when latency budgets are tight.
[09:31] Jordan: great thanks everyone.
[09:34] Alex: recap of next steps: we'll send pricing and security pack, set pilot dates, share demo notebook, and schedule follow-up on 2025-05-21 for JSON edge-cases. Thanks all.

End of transcript.
